arXiv:1706.00440v2 [math-ph] 04 Jan 2018

The conditional Entropy Power Inequality for bosonic quantum systems

Giacomo De Palma Affiliation: QMATH, Department of Mathematical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, Universitetsparken 5, 2100 Copenhagen, Denmark    Dario Trevisan Affiliation: Università degli Studi di Pisa, I-56126 Pisa, Italy
Abstract

We prove the conditional Entropy Power Inequality for Gaussian quantum systems. This fundamental inequality determines the minimum quantum conditional von Neumann entropy of the output of the beam-splitter or of the squeezing among all the input states where the two inputs are conditionally independent given the memory and have given quantum conditional entropies. We also prove that, for any couple of values of the quantum conditional entropies of the two inputs, the minimum of the quantum conditional entropy of the output given by the conditional Entropy Power Inequality is asymptotically achieved by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian input states. Our proof of the conditional Entropy Power Inequality is based on a new Stam inequality for the quantum conditional Fisher information and on the determination of the universal asymptotic behaviour of the quantum conditional entropy under the heat semigroup evolution. The beam-splitter and the squeezing are the central elements of quantum optics, and can model the attenuation, the amplification and the noise of electromagnetic signals. This conditional Entropy Power Inequality will have a strong impact in quantum information and quantum cryptography. Among its many possible applications there is the proof of a new uncertainty relation for the conditional Wehrl entropy.

1 Introduction

The Shannon differential entropy [2] of a random variable XX with values in ℝk\mathbb{R}^{k} and probability density pX​(𝐱)​dk​xp_{X}(\mathbf{x})\mathrm{d}^{k}x is

S(X):=−∫ℝklnpX(𝐱)dpX(𝐱),S(X):=-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{k}}\ln p_{X}(\mathbf{x})\;\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})\;, (1)

and quantifies the noise or the information contained in XX. Let us consider the linear combination

C:=η​A+|1−η|​B,η≥0C:=\sqrt{\eta}\,A+\sqrt{|1-\eta|}\,B\;,\qquad\eta\geq 0 (2)

of two independent random variables AA and BB with values in ℝk\mathbb{R}^{k}. The classical Entropy Power Inequality [13, 22, 21] states that, if AA and BB have Shannon differential entropy fixed to the values S⁡(A)S(A) and S⁡(B)S(B), respectively, the Shannon differential entropy of CC is minimized when AA and BB have a Gaussian probability distribution with proportional covariance matrices:

exp⁡2​S​(C)k≥η​exp⁡2​S​(A)k+|1−η|​exp⁡2​S​(B)k,\exp\frac{2S(C)}{k}\geq\eta\exp\frac{2S(A)}{k}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{2S(B)}{k}\;, (3)

and is a fundamental element of classical information theory [2].

The noncommutative counterpart of probability measures are quantum states, that are linear positive operators on a Hilbert space with unit trace. The counterpart of the probability measures on ℝk\mathbb{R}^{k} with even kk are the quantum states of a Gaussian quantum system with n=k2n=\frac{k}{2} modes. Gaussian quantum systems [16, 17] model electromagnetic waves in the quantum regime. Electromagnetic waves traveling through cables or free space provide the most promising platform for quantum communication and quantum key distribution [23]. Gaussian quantum systems then play a key role in quantum communication and quantum cryptography, and provide the model to determine the maximum communication and key distribution rates achievable in principle by quantum communication devices. The noncommutative counterpart of the linear combination (2) is the beam-splitter of transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 or the squeezing of parameter η≥1\eta\geq 1. The beam-splitter and the squeezing are the fundamental elements of quantum optics, and can model the attenuation, the amplification and the noise of electromagnetic signals.

The quantum counterpart of the Shannon differential entropy is the von Neumann entropy of a quantum state [16, 24]

S⁡(ρ^):=−Tr⁡[ρ^​ln⁡ρ^].S(\hat{\rho}):=-\mathrm{Tr}\left[\hat{\rho}\ln\hat{\rho}\right]\;. (4)

In this paper we prove the conditional Entropy Power Inequality for Gaussian quantum systems (Theorem 6.1). Let AA and BB be the nn-mode Gaussian quantum systems at the input of the beam-splitter of transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 or of the squeezing of parameter η≥1\eta\geq 1, and let CC be the nn-mode Gaussian quantum system at the output. Let us consider a joint quantum input state ρ^A​B​M\hat{\rho}_{ABM} such that AA and BB are conditionally independent given the memory system MM. This condition is expressed with the vanishing of the quantum conditional mutual information:

I(A:B|M):=S(A|M)+S(B|M)−S(AB|M)=0,I(A:B|M):=S(A|M)+S(B|M)-S(AB|M)=0\;, (5)

where

S⁡(X|M):=S⁡(X​M)−S⁡(M)S(X|M):=S(XM)-S(M) (6)

is the quantum conditional entropy. The conditional Entropy Power Inequality determines the minimum quantum conditional entropy of the output S⁡(C|M)S(C|M) among all the quantum input states ρ^A​B​M\hat{\rho}_{ABM} as above and with given quantum conditional entropies S⁡(A|M)S(A|M) and S⁡(B|M)S(B|M):

exp⁡S⁡(C|M)n≥η​exp⁡S⁡(A|M)n+|1−η|​exp⁡S⁡(B|M)n.\exp\frac{S(C|M)}{n}\geq\eta\exp\frac{S(A|M)}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{S(B|M)}{n}\;. (7)

We also prove that, for any couple of values of S⁡(A|M)S(A|M) and S⁡(B|M)S(B|M), the minimum (7) for S⁡(C|M)S(C|M) is asymptotically achieved by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian input states (Theorem 7.1).

The conditional Entropy Power Inequality (7) had been conjectured in [18]. It is the conditional version of the quantum Entropy Power Inequality [6, 5, 19, 20] that provides a lower bound to the von Neumann entropy S⁡(C)S(C) of the output of the beam-splitter or of the squeezing for all the product input states ρ^A​B=ρ^A⊗ρ^B\hat{\rho}_{AB}=\hat{\rho}_{A}\otimes\hat{\rho}_{B} in terms of the entropies of the inputs S⁡(A)S(A) and S⁡(B)S(B):

exp⁡S⁡(C)n≥η​exp⁡S⁡(A)n+|1−η|​exp⁡S⁡(B)n.\exp\frac{S(C)}{n}\geq\eta\exp\frac{S(A)}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{S(B)}{n}\;. (8)

Contrarily to the classical Entropy Power Inequality (3), the quantum Entropy Power Inequality (8) is not saturated by quantum Gaussian states with proportional covariance matrices, unless they have the same entropy [5].

In the classical scenario, the conditional Entropy Power Inequality reads

exp⁡2​S​(C|M)k≥η​exp⁡2​S​(A|M)k+|1−η|​exp⁡2​S​(B|M)k,\exp\frac{2S(C|M)}{k}\geq\eta\exp\frac{2S(A|M)}{k}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{2S(B|M)}{k}\;, (9)

where AA and BB are random variables with values in ℝk\mathbb{R}^{k} and are conditionally independent given the random variable MM, and CC is as in (2). The conditional Entropy Power Inequality (9) is an easy consequence of its unconditioned version (3), because the conditional entropy S⁡(X|M)S(X|M) coincides with the expectation value with respect to MM of the entropy of XX given the value of MM (see Appendix A):

S⁡(X|M)=∫MS⁡(X|M=m)​d​pM​(m).S(X|M)=\int_{M}S(X|M=m)\,\mathrm{d}p_{M}(m)\;. (10)

The classical conditional Entropy Power Inequality (9) is saturated by any joint probability measure on A​B​MABM such that, conditioning on any value mm of MM, AA and BB are independent Gaussian random variables with proportional covariance matrices, and the proportionality constant does not depend on mm.

In the quantum scenario, conditioning on the value of MM is not possible in the presence of entanglement between A​BAB and MM, and the conditional Entropy Power Inequality is not an easy consequence of the unconditioned Entropy Power Inequality. The saturation conditions are another fundamental difference between the classical and the quantum scenario. The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality can be saturated only asymptotically by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian states. Contrarily to the classical scenario, the correlation of the inputs AA and BB with the memory MM is necessary for the saturation of the inequality. Indeed, the unconditioned quantum Entropy Power Inequality is not saturated even asymptotically by quantum Gaussian states.

Entropic inequalities are the main tool to prove upper bounds to quantum communication rates [24, 16] and to prove the security of quantum key distribution schemes [1]. In these scenarios, a prominent role is played by entropic inequalities in the presence of quantum memory, where the entropies are conditioned on the knowledge of an external observer holding a memory quantum system. The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality proven in this paper will have a profound impact in quantum information theory and quantum cryptography. The inequality has been fundamental in the proof of a new uncertainty relation for the conditional Wehrl entropy [3]. In section 8, we exploit the inequality to prove an upper bound to the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a non-Gaussian quantum channel. This implication has been first considered in [18], section III.

The proof of the quantum conditional Entropy Power inequality is based on the evolution with the heat semigroup as in [6, 5, 19, 18]. For simplifying the proof, we reformulate the inequality in the equivalent linear version (106) through the Legendre transform. The linear inequality (106) had been proven with a particular choice of MM for Gaussian input states in [18], Theorem 8.1. Our proof consists of two parts:

  • •

    We prove the quantum conditional Stam inequality (Theorem 4.1), which provides an upper bound to the quantum conditional Fisher information of the output of the beam-splitter or of the squeezing in terms of the quantum conditional Fisher information of the two inputs. This inequality implies that the difference between the two sides of the linear inequality (106) decreases along the evolution with the heat semigroup. The linear version (66) of the quantum conditional Stam inequality in the particular case λ=η\lambda=\eta had been proven in [18], eq. (62). The proof of [18], as well as the proofs of the unconditioned quantum Stam inequality of [6, 5, 19], are affected by regularity issues. Indeed, all these papers define the quantum Fisher information as the Hessian of the relative entropy with respect to the displacements, but they do not prove that this Hessian is well defined. We introduce a new integral version of the conditional quantum Fisher information, and we define the conditional quantum Fisher information as the limit of its integral version. This definition solves all the previous regularity issues. Our proof of the quantum conditional Stam inequality is based on an integral version of the quantum de Bruijn identity (Theorem 3.1), that relates the increase of the quantum conditional entropy generated by the heat semigroup with the integral quantum conditional Fisher information (6).

  • •

    We prove that the quantum conditional entropy has an universal scaling independent on the initial state (Theorem 5.2) in the infinite time limit under the evolution with the heat semigroup. This scaling was already known for Gaussian states ([18], Lemma 6.1) and implies that the linear inequality (106) asymptotically becomes an equality. Our proof is based on a more general result (Theorem 5.1), stating that the minimum quantum conditional entropy of the output of any Gaussian quantum channel is asymptotically achieved by the purification of the thermal quantum Gaussian states with infinite temperature.

The paper is structured as follows. In section 2 we present Gaussian quantum systems, the beam-splitter and the squeezing. In section 3 we present the quantum integral conditional Fisher information, and in section 4 we prove the quantum conditional Stam inequality. In section 5 we prove the universal asymptotic scaling of the quantum conditional entropy. In section 6 we prove the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality, and in section 7 we prove that this inequality is optimal. In section 8 we apply the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality to prove an upper bound to the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of a non-Gaussian quantum channel. We conclude in section 9. Appendix A and Appendix B contain the proof of the classical conditional Entropy Power Inequality and of the auxiliary lemmas, respectively.

2 Gaussian quantum systems

The Hilbert space of a Gaussian quantum system with nn modes is the irreducible representation of the canonical commutation relations

[Q^k,Q^l]=0,[P^k,P^l]=0,[Q^k,P^l]=iδk​l𝕀^,k,l=1,…,n.\left[\hat{Q}^{k},\;\hat{Q}^{l}\right]=0\;,\quad\left[\hat{P}^{k},\;\hat{P}^{l}\right]=0\;,\quad\left[\hat{Q}^{k},\;\hat{P}^{l}\right]=i\,\delta^{kl}\,\hat{\mathbb{I}}\;,\quad k,\,l=1,\,\ldots,\,n\;. (11)

We define

R^2​k−1:=Q^k,R^2​k:=P^k,k=1,…,n,\hat{R}^{2k-1}:=\hat{Q}^{k}\;,\qquad\hat{R}^{2k}:=\hat{P}^{k}\;,\qquad k=1,\,\ldots,\,n\;, (12)

and (11) becomes

[R^i,R^j]=i​Δi​j​𝕀^,i,j=1,…, 2​n,\left[\hat{R}^{i},\;\hat{R}^{j}\right]=i\,\Delta^{ij}\,\hat{\mathbb{I}}\;,\qquad i,\,j=1,\,\ldots,\,2n\;, (13)

where

Δ:=⨁k=1n(01−10)\Delta:=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{n}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}0&1\\ -1&0\\ \end{array}\right) (14)

is the symplectic form. The Hamiltonian of the system is

H^=12​∑i=12​n(R^i)2−n2​𝕀^.\hat{H}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{2n}\left(\hat{R}^{i}\right)^{2}-\frac{n}{2}\,\hat{\mathbb{I}}\;. (15)
Definition 1 (displacement operators)

For any 𝐱∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n} we define the displacement operator

D^​(𝐱):=exp⁡(i​∑i=12​nxi​Δi​j−1​R^j),\hat{D}(\mathbf{x}):=\exp\left(i\sum_{i=1}^{2n}x^{i}\,\Delta^{-1}_{ij}\,\hat{R}^{j}\right)\;, (16)

the unitary operator satisfying for any i=1,…, 2​ni=1,\,\ldots,\,2n

D^​(𝐱)†​R^i​D^​(𝐱)=R^i+xi​𝕀^.{\hat{D}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,\hat{R}^{i}\,\hat{D}(\mathbf{x})=\hat{R}^{i}+x^{i}\,\hat{\mathbb{I}}\;. (17)
Definition 2 (first moments)

The first moments of a quantum state ρ^\hat{\rho} are

ri(ρ^):=Tr[R^iρ^],i=1,…, 2n.r^{i}(\hat{\rho}):=\mathrm{Tr}\left[\hat{R}^{i}\,\hat{\rho}\right]\;,\qquad i=1,\,\ldots,\,2n\;. (18)
Definition 3 (covariance matrix)

The covariance matrix of a quantum state ρ^\hat{\rho} with finite first moments is

σi​j​(ρ^):=12​Tr​[{R^i−ri​(ρ^),R^j−rj​(ρ^)}​ρ^],i,j=1,…, 2​n,\sigma^{ij}(\hat{\rho}):=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{Tr}\left[\left\{\hat{R}^{i}-r^{i}(\hat{\rho}),\;\hat{R}^{j}-r^{j}(\hat{\rho})\right\}\hat{\rho}\right]\;,\qquad i,\,j=1,\,\ldots,\,2n\;, (19)

where

{X^,Y^}:=X^​Y^+Y^​X^\left\{\hat{X},\;\hat{Y}\right\}:=\hat{X}\,\hat{Y}+\hat{Y}\,\hat{X} (20)

is the anticommutator.

Definition 4 (symplectic eigenvalues)

The symplectic eigenvalues of a real positive matrix σ\sigma are the absolute values of the eigenvalues of Δ−1​σ\Delta^{-1}\sigma.

Definition 5 (heat semigroup)

The heat semigroup is the time evolution generated by the convex combination of displacement operators with Gaussian distribution and covariance matrix t​I2​nt\,I_{2n}: for any quantum state ρ^\hat{\rho}

𝒩⁡(t)​(ρ^):=∫ℝ2​nD^​(𝐱)​ρ^​D^​(𝐱)†​e−|𝐱|22​t​d2​n​x(2​π​t)n.\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\rho}):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}\hat{D}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}\,{\hat{D}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{|\mathbf{x}|^{2}}{2t}}\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2n}x}{(2\pi\,t)^{n}}\;. (21)

For any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0

𝒩⁡(s)∘𝒩⁡(t)=𝒩⁡(s+t).\mathcal{N}(s)\circ\mathcal{N}(t)=\mathcal{N}(s+t)\;. (22)

2.1 Quantum Gaussian states

A quantum Gaussian state is a density operator proportional to the exponential of a quadratic polynomial in the quadratures:

γ^=exp(−12∑i,j=12​n(R^i−ri)hi​j(R^j−rj))Trexp(−12∑i,j=12​n(R^i−ri)hi​j(R^j−rj)),\hat{\gamma}=\frac{\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,\,j=1}^{2n}\left(\hat{R}^{i}-r^{i}\right)h_{ij}\left(\hat{R}^{j}-r^{j}\right)\right)}{\mathrm{Tr}\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,\,j=1}^{2n}\left(\hat{R}^{i}-r^{i}\right)h_{ij}\left(\hat{R}^{j}-r^{j}\right)\right)}\;, (23)

where hh is a positive real 2​n×2​n2n\times 2n matrix and 𝐫∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{r}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}. A thermal Gaussian state is a Gaussian state with zero first moments (𝐫=0\mathbf{r}=0) and where the matrix hh is proportional to the identity:

ω^=e−β​H^Tr​e−β​H^,h=β​I2​n,β>0.\hat{\omega}=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}{\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}\;,\qquad h=\beta\,I_{2n}\;,\qquad\beta>0\;. (24)

The von Neumann entropy of a quantum Gaussian state is

S=∑k=1ng⁡(νk−12),S=\sum_{k=1}^{n}g\left(\nu_{k}-\frac{1}{2}\right)\;, (25)

where

g⁡(x):=(x+1)​ln⁡(x+1)−x​ln⁡x,g(x):=\left(x+1\right)\ln\left(x+1\right)-x\ln x\;, (26)

and ν1,…,νn\nu_{1},\,\ldots,\,\nu_{n} are the symplectic eigenvalues of its covariance matrix.

2.2 Beam-splitter and squeezing

Given the nn-mode Gaussian quantum systems AA, BB, CC and DD, the beam-splitter with inputs AA and BB, outputs CC and DD and transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 is implemented by the mixing unitary operator U^η:A​B→C​D\hat{U}_{\eta}:AB\to CD acting on the quadratures as [14]

U^η†​R^Ci​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{R}_{C}^{i}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =η​R^Ai+1−η​R^Bi,\displaystyle=\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{R}_{A}^{i}+\sqrt{1-\eta}\,\hat{R}_{B}^{i}\;, (27a)
U^η†​R^Di​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{R}_{D}^{i}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =−1−ηR^Ai+ηR^Bi,i=1,…, 2n.\displaystyle=-\sqrt{1-\eta}\,\hat{R}_{A}^{i}+\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{R}_{B}^{i}\;,\qquad i=1,\,\ldots,\,2n\;. (27b)

The beam-splitter is a passive element, and does not require energy for functioning. Indeed, the mixing unitary operator preserves the Hamiltonian (15):

U^η​(H^A+H^B)​U^η†=H^C+H^D.\hat{U}_{\eta}\left(\hat{H}_{A}+\hat{H}_{B}\right)\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}=\hat{H}_{C}+\hat{H}_{D}\;. (28)

The squeezing unitary operator with parameter η≥1\eta\geq 1 acts on the quadratures as [14]

U^η†​Q^Ck​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{Q}_{C}^{k}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =η​Q^Ak+η−1​Q^Bk,\displaystyle=\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{Q}_{A}^{k}+\sqrt{\eta-1}\,\hat{Q}_{B}^{k}\;, (29a)
U^η†​P^Ck​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{P}_{C}^{k}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =η​P^Ak−η−1​P^Bk,\displaystyle=\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{P}_{A}^{k}-\sqrt{\eta-1}\,\hat{P}_{B}^{k}\;, (29b)
U^η†​Q^Dk​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{Q}_{D}^{k}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =η−1​Q^Ak+η​Q^Bk,\displaystyle=\sqrt{\eta-1}\,\hat{Q}_{A}^{k}+\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{Q}_{B}^{k}\;, (29c)
U^η†​P^Dk​U^η\displaystyle\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\,\hat{P}_{D}^{k}\,\hat{U}_{\eta} =−η−1P^Ak+ηP^Bk,k=1,…,n.\displaystyle=-\sqrt{\eta-1}\,\hat{P}_{A}^{k}+\sqrt{\eta}\,\hat{P}_{B}^{k}\;,\qquad k=1,\,\ldots,\,n\;. (29d)

The squeezing acts differently on the QkQ^{k} and on the PkP^{k}. Indeed, the squeezing is an active operation that requires energy, and the squeezing unitary operator does not preserve the Hamiltonian (15).

We define for any joint quantum state ρ^A​B\hat{\rho}_{AB} on A​BAB and any η≥0\eta\geq 0

ℬη​(ρ^A​B):=TrD​[U^η​ρ^A​B​U^η†].\mathcal{B}_{\eta}(\hat{\rho}_{AB}):=\mathrm{Tr}_{D}\left[\hat{U}_{\eta}\,\hat{\rho}_{AB}\,\hat{U}_{\eta}^{\dagger}\right]\;. (30)

ℬη\mathcal{B}_{\eta} implements the beam-splitter for 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 and the squeezing for η≥1\eta\geq 1.

Lemma 1 (compatibility with displacements)

We have for any quantum state ρ^A​B\hat{\rho}_{AB} on A​BAB and any 𝐱,𝐲∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{x},\,\mathbf{y}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}

ℬη​(D^A​(𝐱)​D^B​(𝐲)​ρ^A​B​D^A​(𝐱)†​D^B​(𝐲)†)\displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{D}_{B}(\mathbf{y})\,\hat{\rho}_{AB}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,{\hat{D}_{B}(\mathbf{y})}^{\dagger}\right)
=D^C​(η​𝐱+1−η​𝐲)​ℬη​(ρ^A​B)​D^C​(η​𝐱+1−η​𝐲)†\displaystyle=\hat{D}_{C}\left(\sqrt{\eta}\,\mathbf{x}+\sqrt{1-\eta}\,\mathbf{y}\right)\,\mathcal{B}_{\eta}(\hat{\rho}_{AB})\,{\hat{D}_{C}\left(\sqrt{\eta}\,\mathbf{x}+\sqrt{1-\eta}\,\mathbf{y}\right)}^{\dagger} (31)

for the beam-splitter with transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1, and

ℬη​(D^A​(𝐱)​D^B​(𝐲)​ρ^A​B​D^A​(𝐱)†​D^B​(𝐲)†)\displaystyle\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{D}_{B}(\mathbf{y})\,\hat{\rho}_{AB}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,{\hat{D}_{B}(\mathbf{y})}^{\dagger}\right)
=D^C​(η​𝐱+η−1​T​𝐲)​ℬη​(ρ^A​B)​D^C​(η​𝐱+η−1​T​𝐲)†\displaystyle=\hat{D}_{C}\left(\sqrt{\eta}\,\mathbf{x}+\sqrt{\eta-1}\,T\mathbf{y}\right)\,\mathcal{B}_{\eta}(\hat{\rho}_{AB})\,{\hat{D}_{C}\left(\sqrt{\eta}\,\mathbf{x}+\sqrt{\eta-1}\,T\mathbf{y}\right)}^{\dagger} (32)

T:=⨁k=1n(100−1)T:=\bigoplus_{k=1}^{n}\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}1&0\\ 0&-1\\ \end{array}\right) (33)

For any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0

3 Quantum integral conditional Fisher information

In this Section, we define the quantum integral conditional Fisher information that will permit us to prove the regularity of the quantum Fisher information of [19, 6, 5, 18].

Definition 6 (quantum integral conditional Fisher information)

Let AA be a Gaussian quantum system with nn modes, and MM a quantum system. Let ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} be a quantum state on A​MAM. For any t≥0t\geq 0, we define the integral Fisher information of AA conditioned on MM as

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)\displaystyle\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t) :=I(A:X|M)σ^A​M​X​(t)≥0,t>0,\displaystyle:=I(A:X|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}(t)}\geq 0\;,\qquad t>0\;, (35a)
ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(0)\displaystyle\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(0) :=0,\displaystyle:=0\;, (35b)

where XX is a classical Gaussian random variable with values in ℝ2​n\mathbb{R}^{2n} and probability density function

d​pX​(t)​(𝐱)=e−|𝐱|22​t​d2​n​x(2​π​t)n,𝐱∈ℝ2​n,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(t)(\mathbf{x})=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{|\mathbf{x}|^{2}}{2t}}\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2n}x}{(2\pi\,t)^{n}}\;,\qquad\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\;, (36)

and σ^A​M​X​(t)\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}(t) is the quantum state on A​M​XAMX such that its marginal on XX is pX​(t)p_{X}(t) and for any 𝐱∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}

σ^A​M|X=𝐱​(t)=D^A​(𝐱)​ρ^A​M​D^A​(𝐱)†.\hat{\sigma}_{AM|X=\mathbf{x}}(t)=\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{AM}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\;. (37)
Remark 1

The marginal over A​MAM of σ^A​M​X\hat{\sigma}_{AMX} is

σ^A​M=(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M).\hat{\sigma}_{AM}=(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;. (38)

The fundamental property of the quantum integral conditional Fisher information is the relation with the increase in the quantum conditional entropy generated by the heat semigroup.

Theorem 3.1 (quantum integral conditional de Bruijn identity)

The quantum integral conditional Fisher information coincides with the increase of the quantum conditional entropy generated by the heat semigroup: for any t≥0t\geq 0,

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)=S​(A|M)(𝒩A​(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)−S​(A|M)ρ^A​M.\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t)=S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}_{A}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}-S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\;. (39)
Proof
I(A:X|M)σ^A​M​X\displaystyle I(A:X|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}} =S​(A|M)σ^A​M​X−S​(A|M​X)σ^A​M​X\displaystyle=S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}}-S(A|MX)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}}
=S​(A|M)σ^A​M−∫ℝ2​nS​(A|M)σ^A​M|X=𝐱​d​pX​(𝐱)\displaystyle=S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AM}}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AM|X=\mathbf{x}}}\,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})
=S​(A|M)σ^A​M−∫ℝ2​nS​(A|M)ρ^A​M​d​pX​(𝐱)\displaystyle=S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AM}}-\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2n}}S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})
=S​(A|M)σ^A​M−S​(A|M)ρ^A​M.\displaystyle=S(A|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AM}}-S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\;. (40)

The goal of the remainder of this Section is proving that the quantum integral conditional Fisher information is a continuous, increasing and concave function of time (Theorem 3.2). This result will permit us to prove the regularity of the quantum Fisher information.

Lemma 3 (continuity of quantum integral conditional Fisher information)

For any quantum state ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} such that

TrA​[H^A​ρ^A]=E0<∞,S⁡(ρ^M)<∞\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]=E_{0}<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty (41)

we have

limt→0ΔA|M​((𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M))=ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M).\lim_{t\to 0}\Delta_{A|M}((\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM}))=\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;. (42)
Proof

From Theorem 3.1, the claim is equivalent to

limt→0S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)=S​(A|M)ρ^A​M.\lim_{t\to 0}S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}=S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\;. (43)

We will then proceed along the same lines of the proof of the continuity of the entropy in the set of the quantum states with bounded average energy ([16], Lemma 11.8). We have (see e.g. [4], Lemma 2)

limt→0‖(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)−ρ^A​M‖1=0.\lim_{t\to 0}\left\|(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})-\hat{\rho}_{AM}\right\|_{1}=0\;. (44)

Since the quantum entropy is lower semicontinuous ([16], Theorem 11.6) and

S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)=S⁡((𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M))−S⁡(ρ^M),S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}=S((\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM}))-S(\hat{\rho}_{M})\;, (45)

we have

lim inft→0S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)≥S​(A|M)ρ^A​M.\liminf_{t\to 0}S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\geq S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}\;. (46)

On the other hand, we have for any β>0\beta>0 and any 0≤t<ϵ0\leq t<\epsilon

S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)\displaystyle S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})} =β​TrA​[H^A​𝒩​(t)​(ρ^A)]+ln⁡TrA​e−β​H^A\displaystyle=\beta\,\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\mathcal{N}(t)(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right]+\ln\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}
−S((𝒩(t)⊗𝕀M)(ρ^A​M)‖e−β​H^ATrA​e−β​H^A⊗ρ^M)\displaystyle\phantom{=}-S\left((\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left\|\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}{\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}\otimes\hat{\rho}_{M}\right.\right)
=β⁡(E0+n​t)+ln⁡TrA​e−β​H^A\displaystyle=\beta\left(E_{0}+n\,t\right)+\ln\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}
−S((𝒩(t)⊗𝕀M)(ρ^A​M)‖e−β​H^ATrA​e−β​H^A⊗ρ^M),\displaystyle\phantom{=}-S\left((\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left\|\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}{\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}\otimes\hat{\rho}_{M}\right.\right)\;, (47)

where

S(ρ^∥σ^)=Tr[ρ^(lnρ^−lnσ^)]S(\hat{\rho}\|\hat{\sigma})=\mathrm{Tr}\left[\hat{\rho}\left(\ln\hat{\rho}-\ln\hat{\sigma}\right)\right] (48)

is the quantum relative entropy [16]. Since the quantum relative entropy is lower semicontinuous ([16], Theorem 11.6),

lim supt→0S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)\displaystyle\limsup_{t\to 0}S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})} ≤β⁡(E0+n​t)+ln⁡TrA​e−β​H^A\displaystyle\leq\beta\left(E_{0}+n\,t\right)+\ln\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}
−S(ρ^A​M‖e−β​H^ATrA​e−β​H^A⊗ρ^M)\displaystyle\phantom{=}-S\left(\hat{\rho}_{AM}\left\|\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}{\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}_{A}}}\otimes\hat{\rho}_{M}\right.\right)
=S​(A|M)ρ^A​M+β⁡(E0+n​t−TrA​[H^A​ρ^A]),\displaystyle=S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}+\beta\left(E_{0}+n\,t-\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]\right)\;, (49)

and the claim follows taking the limit β→0\beta\to 0.

Lemma 4

For any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0,

ΔA|M((𝒩A(s)⊗𝕀M)(ρ^A​M))(t)=I(A:X|M)(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(σ^A​M​X​(t)),\Delta_{A|M}((\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM}))(t)=I(A:X|M)_{(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}(t))}\;, (50)

where σ^A​M​X​(t)\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}(t) is as in 6.

where XX is as in 6, and τ^A​M​X​(s,t)\hat{\tau}_{AMX}(s,t) is the quantum state on A​M​XAMX such that its marginal on XX is pX​(t)p_{X}(t), and for any 𝐱∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}

τ^A​M|X=𝐱​(s,t)\displaystyle\hat{\tau}_{AM|X=\mathbf{x}}(s,t) =D^A​(𝐱)​(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)​D^A​(𝐱)†\displaystyle=\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}
=(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(D^A​(𝐱)​ρ^A​M​D^A​(𝐱)†)\displaystyle=(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{AM}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\right)
=(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(σ^A​M|X=𝐱​(t)).\displaystyle=(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\sigma}_{AM|X=\mathbf{x}}(t))\;. (52)

Hence for any t≥0t\geq 0

τ^A​M​X​(s,t)=(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(σ^A​M​X​(t)),\hat{\tau}_{AMX}(s,t)=(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\sigma}_{AMX}(t))\;, (53)

and the claim follows.

Lemma 5

For any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0

ΔA|M​((𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M))​(t)≤ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t).\Delta_{A|M}((\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM}))(t)\leq\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t)\;. (54)

that follows from the data-processing inequality for the quantum mutual information.

Lemma 6

For any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s+t)\displaystyle\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(s+t) =ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s)+ΔA|M​((𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M))​(t)\displaystyle=\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(s)+\Delta_{A|M}((\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM}))(t)

Theorem 3.2 (regularity of quantum integral conditional Fisher information)

For any quantum state ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} on A​MAM such that

TrA​[H^A​ρ^A]<∞,S⁡(ρ^M)<∞,\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;, (57)

the quantum integral conditional Fisher information S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})} is a continuous, increasing and concave function of time.

Proof

The continuity follows from 3 and 6. From 6, S​(A|M)(𝒩⁡(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})} is increasing. We then have to prove that for any s,t≥0s,\,t\geq 0

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s+t2)​≥?​ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s)+ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)2.\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left(\frac{s+t}{2}\right)\overset{?}{\geq}\frac{\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(s)+\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t)}{2}\;. (58)

Without lost of generality we can assume s≤ts\leq t. We can rephrase (58) as

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s+t2)−ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s)\displaystyle\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left(\frac{s+t}{2}\right)-\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(s)
≥?​ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)−ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(s+t2),\displaystyle\overset{?}{\geq}\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t)-\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left(\frac{s+t}{2}\right)\;, (59)

that thanks to 6 is equivalent to

ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M​(s))​(t−s2)\displaystyle\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM}(s))\left(\frac{t-s}{2}\right)
≥?​ΔA|M​((𝒩A​(t−s2)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M​(s)))​(t−s2),\displaystyle\overset{?}{\geq}\Delta_{A|M}\left(\left(\mathcal{N}_{A}\left(\frac{t-s}{2}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{AM}(s))\right)\left(\frac{t-s}{2}\right)\;, (60)

where

ρ^A​M​(s):=(𝒩A​(s)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M).\hat{\rho}_{AM}(s):=(\mathcal{N}_{A}(s)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;. (61)

Finally, (60) holds from 5.

4 Quantum conditional Fisher information and quantum Stam inequality

In this Section, we derive the quantum conditional Fisher information and the quantum conditional de Bruijn identity from their integral versions presented in section 3, and we prove that the quantum conditional Fisher information satisfies the quantum Stam inequality.

Definition 7 (quantum conditional Fisher information)

Let ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} be a quantum state on A​MAM satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 3.2. The Fisher information of AA conditioned on MM is

J​(A|M)ρ^A​M:=limt→0ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)t.J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}:=\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t)}{t}\;. (62)
Remark 2

Since from Theorem 3.2 the function t↦ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(t)t\mapsto\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})(t) is continuous and concave, the limit in (62) always exists (finite or infinite).

Remark 3

7is equivalent to the definition of [18], eq. (53).

Proposition 1 (quantum conditional de Bruijn identity)

The quantum conditional Fisher information coincides with the time derivative of the quantum conditional entropy under the heat semigroup evolution:

J​(A|M)ρ^A​M=dd​t​S​(A|M)(𝒩A​(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)|t=0.J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}=\left.\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}S(A|M)_{(\mathcal{N}_{A}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\right|_{t=0}\;. (63)
Proof

Follows from Theorem 3.1.

Remark 4

1had been proven in [18], Theorem 7.3 in the particular case where ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} is a quantum Gaussian state.

Theorem 4.1 (quantum conditional Stam inequality)

Let AA, BB and CC be Gaussian quantum systems with nn modes, MM a quantum system, and ℬη:A​B→C\mathcal{B}_{\eta}:AB\to C the beam-splitter with transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 or the squeezing with parameter η≥1\eta\geq 1. Let ρ^A​B​M\hat{\rho}_{ABM} be a quantum state on A​B​MABM such that

TrA​B​[(H^A+H^B)​ρ^A​B]<∞,S⁡(ρ^M)<∞,\mathrm{Tr}_{AB}\left[\left(\hat{H}_{A}+\hat{H}_{B}\right)\hat{\rho}_{AB}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;, (64)

and let us suppose that AA and BB are conditionally independent given MM:

I(A:B|M)ρ^A​B​M=0,I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}=0\;, (65)

Then, for any 0≤λ≤10\leq\lambda\leq 1 the quantum linear conditional Stam inequality holds:

J​(C|M)ρ^C​M≤λ2η​J​(A|M)ρ^A​M+(1−λ)2|1−η|​J​(B|M)ρ^B​M,J(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}\leq\frac{\lambda^{2}}{\eta}J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}+\frac{(1-\lambda)^{2}}{|1-\eta|}J(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}\;, (66)

where

ρ^C​M:=(ℬη⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​B​M).\hat{\rho}_{CM}:=(\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{ABM})\;. (67)

The quantum conditional Stam inequality follows minimizing over λ\lambda the right-hand side of (66):

1J​(C|M)ρ^C​M≥ηJ​(A|M)ρ^A​M+|1−η|J​(B|M)ρ^B​M.\frac{1}{J(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}}\geq\frac{\eta}{J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}+\frac{|1-\eta|}{J(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}\;. (68)
Remark 5

The linear Stam inequality (66) had been proven in the particular case λ=η\lambda=\eta in [18], eq. (62).

Proof

We will prove the following inequality for the quantum integral conditional Fisher information:

ΔC|M​(ρ^C​M)​(t)≤ΔA|M​(ρ^A​M)​(λ2​tη)+ΔB|M​(ρ^B​M)​((1−λ)2​t|1−η|).\Delta_{C|M}(\hat{\rho}_{CM})(t)\leq\Delta_{A|M}(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}\,t}{\eta}\right)+\Delta_{B|M}(\hat{\rho}_{BM})\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)^{2}\,t}{|1-\eta|}\right)\;. (69)

The quantum linear conditional Stam inequality (66) follows taking the derivative of (69) in t=0t=0. The quantum conditional Stam inequality (68) follows choosing

λ=η​J​(B|M)ρ^B​Mη​J​(B|M)ρ^B​M+|1−η|​J​(A|M)ρ^A​M,\lambda=\frac{\eta\,J(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}{\eta\,J(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}+|1-\eta|\,J(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}\;, (70)

that minimizes the right-hand side of (66).

For any t≥0t\geq 0

ΔC|M(ρ^C​M)(t)=I(C:Z|M)σ^C​M​Z​(t),\Delta_{C|M}(\hat{\rho}_{CM})(t)=I(C:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{CMZ}(t)}\;, (71)

where ZZ is a Gaussian random variable with values in ℝ2​n\mathbb{R}^{2n} and probability density function

d​pZ​(t)​(𝐳)=e−|𝐳|22​t​d2​n​z(2​π​t)n,𝐳∈ℝ2​n,\mathrm{d}p_{Z}(t)(\mathbf{z})=\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{|\mathbf{z}|^{2}}{2t}}\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2n}z}{(2\pi\,t)^{n}}\;,\qquad\mathbf{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}\;, (72)

and σ^C​M​Z​(t)\hat{\sigma}_{CMZ}(t) is the quantum state on C​M​ZCMZ such that its marginal on ZZ is pZ​(t)p_{Z}(t) and for any 𝐳∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}

σ^C​M|Z=𝐳​(t)=D^C​(𝐳)​ρ^C​M​D^C​(𝐳)†.\hat{\sigma}_{CM|Z=\mathbf{z}}(t)=\hat{D}_{C}(\mathbf{z})\,\hat{\rho}_{CM}\,{\hat{D}_{C}(\mathbf{z})}^{\dagger}\;. (73)

We define the quantum state σ^A​B​M​Z​(t)\hat{\sigma}_{ABMZ}(t) on A​B​M​ZABMZ such that its marginal on ZZ is pZ​(t)p_{Z}(t) and for any 𝐳∈ℝ2​n\mathbf{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}

if 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1, and

=D^A​(λ​𝐳η)​D^B​((1−λ)​T​𝐳η−1)​ρ^A​B​M​D^A​(λ​𝐳η)†​D^B​((1−λ)​T​𝐳η−1)†\displaystyle=\hat{D}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta}}\right)\hat{D}_{B}\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)T\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta-1}}\right)\hat{\rho}_{ABM}{\hat{D}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta}}\right)}^{\dagger}{\hat{D}_{B}\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)T\mathbf{z}}{\sqrt{\eta-1}}\right)}^{\dagger} (75)

if η≥1\eta\geq 1, where TT is the time-reversal matrix defined in (33). We then have for any t≥0t\geq 0

=I(A:Z|M)σ^A​M​Z+I(B:Z|M)σ^B​M​Z\displaystyle=I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}}+I(B:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{BMZ}}
+I(A:B|MZ)σ^A​B​M​Z−I(A:B|M)σ^A​B​M\displaystyle\phantom{=}+I(A:B|MZ)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABMZ}}-I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{ABM}}
≤I(A:Z|M)σ^A​M​Z+I(B:Z|M)σ^B​M​Z.\displaystyle\leq I(A:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AMZ}}+I(B:Z|M)_{\hat{\sigma}_{BMZ}}\;. (78)

Proceeding as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 we get

where

=(𝒩A​(λ2​tη)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M),\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{A}\left(\frac{\lambda^{2}\,t}{\eta}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{AM})\;, (80)

hence

We can analogously show that

and (78) becomes the claim (69).

5 Universal asymptotic scaling of quantum conditional entropy

In this Section, we prove that the quantum conditional entropy has a universal asymptotic scaling in the infinite-time limit under the heat semigroup evolution (Theorem 5.2). The proof is based on the following more general result, that provides a new universal lower bound for the conditional entropy of the output of any quantum Gaussian channel.

Let AA, BB be quantum Gaussian systems with mm and nn modes, respectively, and Φ:A→B\Phi:A\to B a quantum Gaussian channel. Let ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} be a quantum state on A​MAM such that

TrA​[H^A​ρ^A]<∞,S⁡(ρ^M)<∞.\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;. (83)

Then, for any quantum system MM and any joint quantum state ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM}

S​(B|M)(Φ⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)≥limν→∞S​(B|A′)(Φ⊗𝕀A′)​(ω^A​A′​(ν)),S(B|M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}\geq\lim_{\nu\to\infty}S(B|A^{\prime})_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}})(\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu))}\;, (84)

where A′A^{\prime} is a Gaussian quantum system with mm modes, and for any ν≥12\nu\geq\frac{1}{2}, ω^A​A′​(ν)\hat{\omega}_{AA^{\prime}}(\nu) is a purification of the thermal Gaussian state ω^A​(ν)\hat{\omega}_{A}(\nu) on AA with covariance matrix ν​I2​m\nu\,I_{2m}.

(85)

≥S⁡(Φ~​(γ^A))−S⁡(γ^A),\displaystyle\geq S\left(\tilde{\Phi}(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\right)-S(\hat{\gamma}_{A})\;, (87)

(91)

For any t>0t>0,

6 Quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality

In this Section we prove the conditional Entropy Power Inequality, the main result of this paper.

Theorem 6.1 (quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality)

Let AA, BB and CC be Gaussian quantum systems with nn modes, MM a quantum system, and ℬη:A​B→C\mathcal{B}_{\eta}:AB\to C the beam-splitter with transmissivity 0≤η≤10\leq\eta\leq 1 or the squeezer of parameter η≥1\eta\geq 1. Let ρ^A​B​M\hat{\rho}_{ABM} be a quantum state on A​B​MABM such that

TrA​B​[(H^A+H^B)​ρ^A​B]<∞,S⁡(ρ^M)<∞,\mathrm{Tr}_{AB}\left[\left(\hat{H}_{A}+\hat{H}_{B}\right)\hat{\rho}_{AB}\right]<\infty\;,\qquad S(\hat{\rho}_{M})<\infty\;, (104)

and let us suppose that AA and BB are conditionally independent given MM:

I(A:B|M)ρ^A​B​M=0.I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}=0\;. (105)

Then, for any 0≤λ≤10\leq\lambda\leq 1 the quantum linear conditional Entropy Power Inequality holds:

S​(C|M)ρ^C​Mn\displaystyle\frac{S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}}{n} ≥λ​S​(A|M)ρ^A​Mn+(1−λ)​S​(B|M)ρ^B​Mn\displaystyle\geq\lambda\,\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}{n}+\left(1-\lambda\right)\frac{S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}{n}
+λ​ln⁡ηλ+(1−λ)​ln⁡|1−η|1−λ.\displaystyle\phantom{\geq}+\lambda\ln\frac{\eta}{\lambda}+(1-\lambda)\ln\frac{|1-\eta|}{1-\lambda}\;. (106)

The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality follows maximizing over λ\lambda the right-hand side of (106):

exp⁡S​(C|M)ρ^C​Mn≥η​exp⁡S​(A|M)ρ^A​Mn+|1−η|​exp⁡S​(B|M)ρ^B​Mn.\exp\frac{S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}}}{n}\geq\eta\,\exp\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}}}{n}\;. (107)
Remark 7

The quantum linear inequality (106) had been proven for λ=η\lambda=\eta in the special case where ρ^A​B​M\hat{\rho}_{ABM} is a quantum Gaussian state in [18], Theorem 8.1.

Proof

Let us define for any t≥0t\geq 0

ρ^B​M​(t)\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t) =(𝒩B​((1−λ)​t|1−η|)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^B​M),\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{B}\left(\frac{(1-\lambda)\,t}{|1-\eta|}\right)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{BM})\;, (109b)
ρ^C​M​(t)\displaystyle\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t) =(𝒩C​(t)⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^C​M),\displaystyle=\left(\mathcal{N}_{C}(t)\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M}\right)(\hat{\rho}_{CM})\;, (109c)

where we have set ρ^C​M:=ρ^C​M​(0)\hat{\rho}_{CM}:=\hat{\rho}_{CM}(0). The time evolution preserves the condition I(A:B|M)=0I(A:B|M)=0. Indeed, we have from the data-processing inequality for the quantum mutual information

0≤I(A:B|M)ρ^A​B​M​(t)≤I(A:B|M)ρ^A​B​M=0.0\leq I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}(t)}\leq I(A:B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{ABM}}=0\;. (110)

=limt→∞(S​(C|M)ρ^C​M​(t)−λ​S​(A|M)ρ^A​M​(t)−(1−λ)​S​(B|M)ρ^B​M​(t))\displaystyle=\lim_{t\to\infty}\left(S(C|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{CM}(t)}-\lambda\,S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}(t)}-(1-\lambda)\,S(B|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{BM}(t)}\right)
=n⁡(λ​ln⁡ηλ+(1−λ)​ln⁡|1−η|1−λ),\displaystyle=n\left(\lambda\ln\frac{\eta}{\lambda}+\left(1-\lambda\right)\ln\frac{|1-\eta|}{1-\lambda}\right)\;, (114)

and the quantum linear conditional Entropy Power Inequality (106) follows. The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality (107) follows choosing

that maximizes the right-hand side of (106).

7 Optimality of the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality

In this Section, we prove that the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality is asymptotically saturated by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian input states.

Theorem 7.1 (optimality of the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality)

The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality (107) is optimal. In other words, for any a,b∈ℝa,\,b\in\mathbb{R} there exists a sequence of quantum Gaussian input states {γ^A​B​A′​B′(n)}n∈ℕ\left\{\hat{\gamma}_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}\right\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}} of the form

γ^A​B​A′​B′(n)=γ^A​A′(n)⊗γ^B​B′(n),n∈ℕ,\hat{\gamma}_{ABA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}=\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)}\otimes\hat{\gamma}_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)}\;,\qquad n\in\mathbb{N}\;, (116)

such that

limn→∞exp⁡(S​(A|A′​B′)γ^A​A′​B′(n)−1)\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(A|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right) =a,\displaystyle=a\;, (117a)
limn→∞exp⁡(S​(B|A′​B′)γ^B​A′​B′(n)−1)\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(B|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{BA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right) =b\displaystyle=b (117b)

and

limn→∞exp⁡(S​(C|A′​B′)γ^C​A′​B′(n)−1)=η​a+|1−η|​b,\lim_{n\to\infty}\exp\left(S(C|A^{\prime}B^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{CA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}}-1\right)=\eta\,a+\left|1-\eta\right|b\;, (118)

where

γ^C​A′​B′(n):=(ℬη⊗𝕀A′​B′)​(γ^A​A′(n)⊗γ^B​B′(n)),\hat{\gamma}_{CA^{\prime}B^{\prime}}^{(n)}:=\left(\mathcal{B}_{\eta}\otimes\mathbb{I}_{A^{\prime}B^{\prime}}\right)\left(\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)}\otimes\hat{\gamma}_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)}\right)\;, (119)

and AA, A′A^{\prime}, BB, B′B^{\prime} and CC are one-mode Gaussian quantum systems.

Proof

Let γ^A​A′(n)\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)} and γ^B​B′(n)\hat{\gamma}_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)} be the quantum Gaussian states with covariance matrices

σB​B′(n)\displaystyle\sigma_{BB^{\prime}}^{(n)} =n⁡(nb0n2b2−100nb0−n2b2−1n2b2−10nb00−n2b2−10nb),\displaystyle=n\left(\begin{array}[]{cc|cc}\frac{n}{b}&0&\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}}{b^{2}}-1}&0\\ 0&\frac{n}{b}&0&-\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}}{b^{2}}-1}\\ \hline\cr\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}}{b^{2}}-1}&0&\frac{n}{b}&0\\ 0&-\sqrt{\frac{n^{2}}{b^{2}}-1}&0&\frac{n}{b}\\ \end{array}\right)\;,

where the block decompositions refer to the bipartitions A​A′AA^{\prime} and B​B′BB^{\prime}, respectively. The symplectic eigenvalues of σA​A′(n)\sigma_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)} are (n,n)(n,\,n), hence

S​(A​A′)γ^A​A′(n)\displaystyle S(AA^{\prime})_{\hat{\gamma}_{AA^{\prime}}^{(n)}} =2​g​(n−12)=ln⁡n2+2+𝒪⁡(1n2),\displaystyle=2\,g\left(n-\frac{1}{2}\right)=\ln n^{2}+2+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{1}{n^{2}}\right)\;, (121a)

Analogously,

8 Entanglement-assisted classical capacity

In this section, we exploit the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality to prove an upper bound to the entanglement-assisted classical capacity of the following non-Gaussian quantum channel. This implication has been first considered in [18], section III.

Let us fix a quantum state σ^B\hat{\sigma}_{B} on the nn-mode Gaussian quantum system BB. We consider the channel Φ:A→C\Phi:A\to C that mixes with σ^B\hat{\sigma}_{B} the input state ρ^A\hat{\rho}_{A} on the nn-mode Gaussian quantum system AA through a beam-splitter or a squeezing operation:

Φ⁡(ρ^A)=ℬη​(ρ^A⊗σ^B),η≥0.\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A})=\mathcal{B}_{\eta}(\hat{\rho}_{A}\otimes\hat{\sigma}_{B})\;,\qquad\eta\geq 0\;. (132)

If the sender can use an unlimited amount of energy, the entanglement-assisted classical capacity is infinite. Since this scenario is not physical, we assume that the sender can use at most an energy EE per each mode. The entanglement-assisted classical capacity [16, 24] of Φ\Phi is then equal to the supremum of the quantum mutual information:

Ce​a(Φ)=sup{I(C:M)(Φ⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M):ρ^A​M pure,TrA[H^Aρ^A]≤nE}.C_{ea}(\Phi)=\sup\left\{I(C:M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}:\hat{\rho}_{AM}\text{ pure},\;\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]\leq n\,E\right\}\;. (133)

Let

E0:=1n​TrB​[H^B​σ^B],S0:=S⁡(σ^B)nE_{0}:=\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{Tr}_{B}\left[\hat{H}_{B}\,\hat{\sigma}_{B}\right]\;,\qquad S_{0}:=\frac{S(\hat{\sigma}_{B})}{n} (134)

be the average energy and the entropy per mode of σ^B\hat{\sigma}_{B}, respectively. The average energy per mode of Φ⁡(ρ^A)\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}) is

1n​TrC​[H^C​Φ​(ρ^A)]\displaystyle\frac{1}{n}\mathrm{Tr}_{C}\left[\hat{H}_{C}\,\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A})\right] =ηn​TrA​[H^A​ρ^A]+|1−η|​E0+η+|1−η|−12\displaystyle=\frac{\eta}{n}\mathrm{Tr}_{A}\left[\hat{H}_{A}\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\right]+|1-\eta|\,E_{0}+\frac{\eta+|1-\eta|-1}{2}
≤η​E+|1−η|​E0+η+|1−η|−12.\displaystyle\leq\eta\,E+|1-\eta|\,E_{0}+\frac{\eta+|1-\eta|-1}{2}\;. (135)

From 9,

S⁡(Φ⁡(ρ^A))≤n​g​(η​E+|1−η|​E0+η+|1−η|−12).S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))\leq n\;g\left(\eta\,E+|1-\eta|\,E_{0}+\frac{\eta+|1-\eta|-1}{2}\right)\;. (136)

From the quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality we have (we recall that MM is correlated only with AA and that ρ^A​M\hat{\rho}_{AM} is pure)

exp⁡S​(C|M)(Φ⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)n\displaystyle\exp\frac{S(C|M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}}{n} ≥η​exp⁡S​(A|M)ρ^A​Mn+|1−η|​exp⁡S0\displaystyle\geq\eta\exp\frac{S(A|M)_{\hat{\rho}_{AM}}}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp S_{0}
=η​exp⁡−S⁡(ρ^A)n+|1−η|​exp⁡S0\displaystyle=\eta\exp\frac{-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})}{n}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp S_{0}
≥η​exp⁡(−g⁡(E))+|1−η|​exp⁡S0,\displaystyle\geq\eta\exp(-g(E))+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp S_{0}\;, (137)

where in the last step we have used 9 again. Finally,

I​(C:M)(Φ⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)\displaystyle I(C:M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})} =S⁡(Φ⁡(ρ^A))−S​(C|M)(Φ⊗𝕀M)​(ρ^A​M)\displaystyle=S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))-S(C|M)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{M})(\hat{\rho}_{AM})}
≤n​g​(η​E+|1−η|​E0+η+|1−η|−12)\displaystyle\leq n\;g\left(\eta\,E+|1-\eta|\,E_{0}+\frac{\eta+|1-\eta|-1}{2}\right)
−n​ln⁡(η​e−g⁡(E)+|1−η|​eS0),\displaystyle\phantom{\leq}-n\ln\left(\eta\,\mathrm{e}^{-g(E)}+\left|1-\eta\right|\mathrm{e}^{S_{0}}\right)\;, (138)

so that

Ce​a​(Φ)\displaystyle C_{ea}(\Phi) ≤n​g​(η​E+|1−η|​E0+η+|1−η|−12)\displaystyle\leq n\;g\left(\eta\,E+|1-\eta|\,E_{0}+\frac{\eta+|1-\eta|-1}{2}\right)
−n​ln⁡(η​e−g⁡(E)+|1−η|​eS0).\displaystyle\phantom{\leq}-n\ln\left(\eta\,\mathrm{e}^{-g(E)}+\left|1-\eta\right|\mathrm{e}^{S_{0}}\right)\;. (139)

9 Conclusions

We have proven the conditional Entropy Power Inequality for Gaussian quantum systems, which are the most promising platform for quantum communication and quantum key distribution. This fundamental inequality determines the minimum quantum conditional entropy of the output of the beam-splitter or of the squeezing among all the quantum input states where the two inputs are conditionally independent given the memory and have given quantum conditional entropies. This inequality is optimal, since it is asymptotically saturated by a suitable sequence of quantum Gaussian input states. In the unconditioned case, the optimal inequality is still an open challenging conjecture [15] that is turning out to be very hard to prove [9, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12]. The quantum conditional Entropy Power Inequality instead definitively settles the problem in the conditioned case.

Appendix A Proof of the classical conditional Entropy Power Inequality

We have from the definition of the classical conditional entropy

S⁡(C|M)=∫MS⁡(C|M=m)​d​pM​(m),S(C|M)=\int_{M}S(C|M=m)\,\mathrm{d}p_{M}(m)\;, (140)

where pMp_{M} is the probability distribution of MM. From the classical Entropy Power Inequality (3) we have for any mm

S⁡(C|M=m)≥k2​ln⁡(η​exp⁡2​S​(A|M=m)k+|1−η|​exp⁡2​S​(B|M=m)k).S(C|M=m)\geq\frac{k}{2}\ln\left(\eta\exp\frac{2S(A|M=m)}{k}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{2S(B|M=m)}{k}\right)\;. (141)

Finally, since the function

(a,b)↦k2​ln⁡(η​exp⁡2​ak+|1−η|​exp⁡2​bk),a,b∈ℝ\left(a,\,b\right)\mapsto\frac{k}{2}\ln\left(\eta\exp\frac{2a}{k}+\left|1-\eta\right|\exp\frac{2b}{k}\right)\;,\qquad a,\,b\in\mathbb{R} (142)

is convex, we have from (140), (141) and Jensen’s inequality

S⁡(C|M)\displaystyle S(C|M) ≥∫Mk2​ln⁡(η​e2k​S​(A|M=m)+|1−η|​e2k​S​(B|M=m))​d​pM​(m)\displaystyle\geq\int_{M}\frac{k}{2}\ln\left(\eta\,\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}S(A|M=m)}+\left|1-\eta\right|\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}S(B|M=m)}\right)\mathrm{d}p_{M}(m)
≥k2​ln⁡(η​e2k​∫MS⁡(A|M=m)​d​pM​(m)+|1−η|​e2k​∫MS⁡(B|M=m)​d​pM​(m))\displaystyle\geq\frac{k}{2}\ln\left(\eta\,\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}\int_{M}S(A|M=m)\mathrm{d}p_{M}(m)}+\left|1-\eta\right|\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}\int_{M}S(B|M=m)\mathrm{d}p_{M}(m)}\right)
=k2​ln⁡(η​e2k​S​(A|M)+|1−η|​e2k​S​(B|M)).\displaystyle=\frac{k}{2}\ln\left(\eta\,\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}S(A|M)}+\left|1-\eta\right|\mathrm{e}^{\frac{2}{k}S(B|M)}\right)\;. (143)

The conditional Entropy Power Inequality (9) is saturated iff all the inequalities in (143) are equalities. The first inequality is saturated iff, conditioning on any value mm of MM, AA and BB are independent Gaussian random variables with proportional covariance matrices. The second inequality is saturated iff S⁡(A|M=m)−S⁡(B|M=m)S(A|M=m)-S(B|M=m) does not depend on mm. For AA and BB as above, this is equivalent to having the proportionality constant between their covariance matrices independent on mm.

Appendix B

Lemma 8 ([16], Lemma 12.25)

Let ρ^\hat{\rho} be a quantum state on a Gaussian quantum system with finite average energy, and let γ^\hat{\gamma} be the Gaussian quantum state with the same first and second moments. Then

S(γ^)=S(ρ^)+S(ρ^∥γ^).S(\hat{\gamma})=S(\hat{\rho})+S(\hat{\rho}\|\hat{\gamma})\;. (144)
Lemma 9

Let ρ^\hat{\rho} be a quantum state on a Gaussian quantum system with finite average energy, and let ω^\hat{\omega} be the thermal Gaussian quantum state with the same average energy. Then

S⁡(ω^)≥S⁡(ρ^).S(\hat{\omega})\geq S(\hat{\rho})\;. (145)
Proof

Let β>0\beta>0 be such that

ω^=e−β​H^Tr​e−β​H^.\hat{\omega}=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}{\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\beta\hat{H}}}\;. (146)

We then have

S(ω^)=S(ρ^)+S(ρ^∥ω^)+βTr[H^(ω^−ρ^)]≥S(ρ^).S(\hat{\omega})=S(\hat{\rho})+S(\hat{\rho}\|\hat{\omega})+\beta\,\mathrm{Tr}\left[\hat{H}\left(\hat{\omega}-\hat{\rho}\right)\right]\geq S(\hat{\rho})\;. (147)
Lemma 10

Let AA and BB be Gaussian quantum systems with mm and nn modes, respectively, and Φ:A→B\Phi:A\to B a Gaussian quantum channel. Let ρ^A\hat{\rho}_{A} be a quantum state on AA, and pXp_{X} a probability measure on ℝ2​m\mathbb{R}^{2m}. We define

σ^A:=∫ℝ2​mD^A​(𝐱)​ρ^A​D^A​(𝐱)†​d​pX​(𝐱).\hat{\sigma}_{A}:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\,\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})\;. (148)

Then,

S⁡(Φ⁡(ρ^A))−S⁡(ρ^A)≥S⁡(Φ⁡(σ^A))−S⁡(σ^A).S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))-S(\hat{\rho}_{A})\geq S(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A}))-S(\hat{\sigma}_{A})\;. (149)
Proof

Let σ^A​X\hat{\sigma}_{AX} be the joint state on A​XAX such that its marginal on XX is pXp_{X}, and for any 𝐱∈ℝ2​m\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2m}

σ^A|X=𝐱=D^A​(𝐱)​ρ^A​D^A​(𝐱)†.\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}}=\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\;. (150)

We notice that the marginal of σ^A​X\hat{\sigma}_{AX} on AA is σ^A\hat{\sigma}_{A}, and

S​(A|X)σ^A​X\displaystyle S(A|X)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AX}} =∫ℝ2​mS⁡(σ^A|X=𝐱)​d​pX​(𝐱)=S⁡(ρ^A),\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}S\left(\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}}\right)\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})=S(\hat{\rho}_{A})\;, (151)
S​(B|X)(Φ⊗𝕀X)​(σ^A​X)\displaystyle S(B|X)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{X})(\hat{\sigma}_{AX})} =∫ℝ2​mS⁡(Φ⁡(σ^A|X=𝐱))​d​pX​(𝐱)=S⁡(Φ⁡(ρ^A)),\displaystyle=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{2m}}S\left(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A|X=\mathbf{x}})\right)\mathrm{d}p_{X}(\mathbf{x})=S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A}))\;, (152)

where in the last step we used that for any 𝐱∈ℝ2​m\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{2m}

Φ⁡(D^A​(𝐱)​ρ^A​D^A​(𝐱)†)=D^B​(K​𝐱)​Φ​(ρ^A)​D^B​(K​𝐱)†\Phi\left(\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})\,\hat{\rho}_{A}\,{\hat{D}_{A}(\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger}\right)=\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})\,\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A})\,{\hat{D}_{B}(K\mathbf{x})}^{\dagger} (153)

for some matrix K:ℝ2​m→ℝ2​nK:\mathbb{R}^{2m}\to\mathbb{R}^{2n}. We then have

S⁡(σ^A)−S⁡(ρ^A)\displaystyle S(\hat{\sigma}_{A})-S(\hat{\rho}_{A}) =I​(A:X)σ^A​X,\displaystyle=I(A:X)_{\hat{\sigma}_{AX}}\;, (154)
S⁡(Φ⁡(σ^A))−S⁡(Φ⁡(ρ^A))\displaystyle S(\Phi(\hat{\sigma}_{A}))-S(\Phi(\hat{\rho}_{A})) =I​(B:X)(Φ⊗𝕀X)​(σ^A​X),\displaystyle=I(B:X)_{(\Phi\otimes\mathbb{I}_{X})(\hat{\sigma}_{AX})}\;, (155)

and the claim follows from the data-processing inequality for the mutual information.

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

  • Click the "Report Issue" () button, located in the page header.

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.

Our team has already identified the following issues. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for all.

Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a list of packages that need conversion, and welcome developer contributions.
